title: Native Windows High Contrast evidence for the Issue 418 Dialog/Popover prototype

browserObservations.documentTitle: v3 opt-in tokens and theme ownership experiment | Bluent

interactionMethod.browser: Chromium DevTools Protocol against the real Edge page

capture.content: Raw CDP screenshot captured with the Popover probe open while native High Contrast White was active.

limitations: One Windows 11 Pro build and one Microsoft Edge version only; this is not a cross-browser or cross-Windows-scheme matrix.
The only native scheme exercised was High Contrast White. High Contrast Black and user-defined contrast themes were not tested.
The native Windows flag was enabled for this short test and restored to the exact original flags and scheme in a finally block; post-run verification read flags=126 and High Contrast White.

DOM, computed CSS and browser-level CDP keyboard/pointer observations are recorded. The keyboard events were not physical hardware key presses, and no Dialog/Popover UI Automation tree walk was performed during this run.
No Narrator, NVDA or VoiceOver spoken output was captured or evaluated.
The Dialog focus observations include initial focus, one Tab, one Shift+Tab and Escape/focus return. This is not exhaustive forward/backward focus-wrap coverage.
The Popover trigger exposes aria-expanded and aria-controls; the observed SECTION surface has no explicit role. This records prototype output and does not decide the future public contract.

The measured Popover surface element has a transparent computed background. This is scoped to that element; the test did not infer the full ancestor/portal composite surface or a final contrast ratio.
The PNG is a raw browser capture and was not independently pixel-reviewed. It is not visual design acceptance.

This is prototype evidence only. It does not approve the Penpot boards, token schema, semantic allow-list, production CSS aliases, Dialog/Popover API, Focus host contract or any general product support claim.
